prompt: Write applyAndClose so a finally block always logs "close" yet never hides the returned balance or the overdraft exception, then use it from applyAll to skip rejected deltas.
explanation: A finally block runs on every exit path -- normal return, thrown exception, even an early return -- which makes it the right home for cleanup. What it must not do is return or throw: a return inside finally overwrites the value the try block already computed and silently drops an exception that was propagating, so the caller never learns the operation failed. Keeping finally to side effects only (here, appending to the log) preserves both the result and the failure.
hints: Put the log.add("apply " + delta) call and the overdraft check inside the try, and only log.add("close") inside finally.
The return statement belongs in the try block. Do not put a return in finally -- it would replace the balance and discard the exception.
applyAll wraps each applyAndClose call in try/catch (IllegalArgumentException) and leaves the running balance unchanged when the catch fires.
